title: A stack can be a fixed size and its rows fill it
goal: Right now a stack is always exactly as big as whatever is inside it, so you cannot say a menu is 320 points wide and have every row stretch to that width unless you build it on a screen. This adds a size of its own to a group that arranges itself, so a stack can be told how wide it is and its contents fill it.
notes: Follows 2026-09-03 groups-arrange-their-own-contents. Today GroupFlow uses a container box only when group.isFrame; the shortest version is a hug/fixed flag on GroupLayout that gives a plain group a box too, feeding the same contentBox path. Watch idempotence: the cross extent currently comes from the widest child, and a fixed box replaces it.
acceptance: A stack can be given a width and a height, typed, and holds them when its contents change
A row set to stretch fills the stack width rather than the widest row
Setting a stack back to sizing itself leaves its contents exactly where they are
Padding works on a stack that has a size of its own, not only on a screen

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock's per-child hug/fill/fixed control stays cut (the Horizontal/Vertical rows already say it), and distribution stays cut (nothing to spread until a stack is longer than its contents). Two things the task did not ask for turned out to be required for the feature to make sense: (1) typing W or dragging a handle on a stack used to SCALE its contents and then re-flow them with the original gap, which matched nothing, so a resize of an arranged group now sizes it instead; (2) a stack given a size needs a way back, so the Layout section gained Width and Height as Hug/Fixed rows.

Built: GroupLayout.width/.height (nil = hug, no key written when unset), Layer.localBounds gives an arranged group its own box, GroupFlow.Bounds shares out per-axis room (frames unchanged: their box still wins), LayerScaling.rearranging pins only the axis that actually changed and re-flows, and setGroupLayout stops pulling contents to the corner for a group that already arranges itself (that was walking a padded stack across the canvas on every kind switch).
Padding now works on any arranged group, not only a screen: contents start one padding in and the hug box grows by it on both sides.

Verified: 47 tests in the group-layout suite (13 new), full suite 2297 green, and a real walk on the probe (Scripts/playtest/stack-size-walk.json, Screen Recording granted) showing 320 typed into W, rows filling after Horizontal Stretch, padding of 16 on a plain group, and one undo taking a fixed height back to hug.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-stack-size.json with two window captures.

A stack can be given a width and a height (Layout section Width/Height rows, Hug or Fixed; the number is typed in W and H or dragged with a handle), rows set to Stretch fill it, and padding now works on any arranged group. Verified by 13 new core tests (2297 green) and a real probe walk with window captures; audit at queue/audits/2026-09-03-stack-size.json. Pushed to main as 64bbf9d.
